tex_content.label: Hamlemma
tex_content.html:
Given $D > 0$, there is a number $a_0 > 0$ so that for any $a \in (0,a_0)$, if $\diam (Z) = a$ and $t$ is sufficiently large then $\int _{\D N_t}\kappa _{\D N_t}ds \: \le \: \frac{D}{2}$ and $\length (\D N_t) \: \le \: \frac{D}{2} \: \sqrt{t}$, where $\kappa _{\D N_t}$ is the geodesic curvature of $\D N_t \subset N_t$.

Proof

\sketch Argue by contradiction and rescale at the first failure. Hamilton–Ivey pinching, noncollapsing, and compactness yield a $\kappa $-solution or standard-solution limit, contradicting the failure. ↗ prop:kl-hyperbolic-rigidity-stabilization-thick-part-monotonicity-thick-thin-geometry The retained proof uses \cite[Sections 11 and 12]{Hamiltonn}, \cite[Section 12]{Hamiltonn}.

□

Lemma
[existence for diameter]

\label{Hamlemma}
Given $D > 0$, there is a number $a_0 > 0$
so that for any $a \in (0,a_0)$, if $\diam(Z) = a$ and $t$ is
sufficiently large then
$\int_{\D N_t}\kappa_{\D N_t}ds \: \le \: \frac{D}{2}$ and
$\length(\D N_t) \: \le \: \frac{D}{2} \: \sqrt{t}$,
where $\kappa_{\D N_t}$ is the geodesic curvature of
$\D N_t \subset N_t$.
\end{lemma}
